title: Beyond digital twins: the role of foundation models in enhancing the interpretability of multiomics modalities in precision medicine
justification: Although it discusses Medical Digital Twins and interpretability, the abstract explicitly identifies the work as a review article (secondary study), which meets Phase 1 exclusion criterion EC3.

title: A survey of cognitive digital twin and the potential use of LLMs
justification: Although it is about Digital Twins (specifically Cognitive Digital Twins), the paper is explicitly a systematic review/survey (secondary study), which is excluded under EC3 for Phase 1.

title: Digital Convergence in Dental Informatics: A Structured Narrative Review of Artificial Intelligence, Internet of Things, Digital Twins, and Large Language Models with Security, Privacy, and Ethical Perspectives
justification: Although the title/abstract mention Digital Twins and discuss trust/transparency/ethics, this paper is explicitly a narrative/structured review (secondary study), which is excluded in Phase 1 under EC3.

title: A Framework for Standardizing the Development of Serious Games with Real-Time Self-Adaptation Capabilities Using Digital Twins
justification: The paper centrally uses Digital Twins to enable real-time self-adaptation in serious games (IC1). title: An Integrated Approach to Real-Time 3D Sensor Data Visualization for Digital Twin Applications
justification: Digital Twin is central (real-time 3D sensor data visualization for digital twin applications). The work emphasizes intuitive understanding, at-a-glance comprehension, user-selectable visualization options, and enhanced data interpretability—human-centered/interaction and interpretability aspects within a DT context, satisfying Phase 1 IC1 and IC2.

title: SmartGridAgent: An Educational Framework for Reliable Digital Twin-Based Smart Grid Workforce Training with Locally Hosted LLMs
justification: The title indicates a “Digital Twin-Based” smart grid training framework (IC1 likely), and the abstract discusses trustworthiness of LLMs and workforce training/human-centered education aspects (IC2 via human interaction/trust). However, it does not explicitly mention explainability/interpretability/XAI, so relevance to explainability is unclear; retain for later phases.

title: A systematic review of AI as a digital twin for prostate cancer care
justification: Although it is about Digital Twins and explicitly mentions a need for improved explainability, the paper is a systematic review (secondary study), which is excluded in Phase 1 under EC3.

title: Healthcare system optimization using digital twin
justification: Digital twin is a central concept in a healthcare monitoring/optimization system (IC1). The paper emphasizes interpretability for clinicians via a GUI that visually represents patient criticality to support decision-making, indicating human interaction and transparency aspects in the digital twin context (IC2).

title: Advanced User Interaction with Urban Digital Twins using Large Language Models
justification: The paper explicitly proposes a framework for interacting with an Urban Digital Twin using LLMs (IC1) and focuses on user interaction via natural-language querying by diverse stakeholders, narrowing the gap for non-expert users and supporting decision-making (human-centered interaction aspects satisfying IC2).

title: Implementing an AI-Based Digital Twin Analysis System for Real-Time Decision Support in a Custom-Made Sportswear SME
justification: Meets IC1 by centering on an AI-enhanced Digital Twin analysis system for real-time decision support in manufacturing. title: Agentic AI for Cultural Heritage: Embedding Risk Memory in Semantic Digital Twins
justification: The paper explicitly uses semantic Digital Twins (“Semantic Digital Twins” in title; ontology-based framework) and discusses transparency/justification via “structured, explainable reasoning” for decision-making and policy responses, satisfying IC1 and IC2.

title: Theories and Technologies of Intelligent Digital Twin Modeling for Optical Networks (Invited)
justification: Digital Twin is clearly central (intelligent digital twin modeling for optical networks). Potential relevance to interpretability/trustworthiness suggests keeping for later screening.

title: Enhancing medical digital twins within metaverse using blockchain, NFTs and LLMs
justification: Digital Twins are central (medical digital twins) and the paper explicitly addresses human interaction aspects via a metaverse environment and an LLM-powered NPC providing intelligent real-time user interactions and personalized insights, satisfying IC1 and IC2 (human-centered interaction related to the digital twin).

title: Integrating Machine Learning and Characterization in Battery Research: Toward Cognitive Digital Twins with Physics and Knowledge
justification: Although it centers on (cognitive) Digital Twins for batteries, it is explicitly a review article (secondary study), which meets EC3 for exclusion in Phase 1 despite mentions of interpretability/transparent digital twin technologies.

title: Physics-informed digital twin design for supporting the selection of process settings in continuous manufacturing, with a focus in fiberboard production
justification: Meets IC1 by explicitly proposing and applying a digital twin framework for continuous manufacturing. Meets IC2 through multiple human-centered and interpretability aspects: discusses operator decision-making, human-centric constraints, workload trade-offs, and proposes an interpretable model architecture to support informed decisions.

title: Metaverse and Digital Twins in the Age of AI and Extended Reality
justification: The paper centrally discusses Digital Twins and their convergence with the Metaverse. It explicitly addresses interactivity, immersive user experiences, multi-user engagement, and human-centered collaboration via XR/AI/LLM agents within DT environments, satisfying DT relevance plus human-interaction aspects (IC1 + IC2).

title: Models vs infrastructures? On the role of digital twins’ hype in anticipating the governance of the UK energy industry
justification: Digital twins are the central topic (hype, governance, models vs infrastructures in UK energy). The abstract explicitly mentions transparency and public engagement and discusses sociotechnical/ethical-political issues beyond modelling concerns (including explainability), satisfying DT relevance plus human-centered/interaction and transparency aspects (IC1+IC2).

title: Innovative AI strategies for enhancing smart building operations through digital twins: A survey
justification: Although it is clearly about Digital Twins in smart buildings, this is a survey/secondary study (EC3) and the abstract does not mention explainability/interpretability/transparency or human-interaction aspects, focusing instead on AI techniques for prediction/anomaly detection/optimization (EC2).

title: Deep Learning Approaches to Natural Language Processing for Digital Twins of Patients in Psychiatry and Neurological Rehabilitation
justification: The article explicitly focuses on creating Digital Twins of patients using deep learning/NLP (IC1) and directly mentions the need for explainability along with ethical and trust considerations in clinical settings, implying human-centered interaction and transparency aspects (IC2).

title: Redefining Research Crowdsourcing Incorporating Human Feedback with LLM-Powered Digital Twins
justification: Digital twins are central (LLM-powered personalized worker digital twins) and the study explicitly addresses human-in-the-loop interaction plus transparency, ethics, and worker agency, satisfying IC1 and IC2.

justification: The paper clearly centers on Enterprise Digital Twins (IC1) and emphasizes reducing cognitive burden and coordinating domain experts/stakeholders via LLMs and MDE, which suggests human-centered interaction aspects. title: Agentic AI for Digital Twin
justification: Digital Twin is central (agentic LLM-powered digital twin for shipping) and it emphasizes a natural-language interface for various stakeholders (human interaction). justification: The article centrally proposes a web-based hybrid Digital Twin platform for EV battery capacity estimation (IC1) and explicitly reports using explainable AI (XAI) techniques to select the most trustworthy and explainable model (IC2), clearly meeting Phase 1 inclusion.

justification: The abstract clearly centers on a Digital Twin ecosystem/framework for water reserve management (IC1) and emphasizes human/decision-support and participatory stakeholder decision-making via immersive simulations and AI-DSS/RAG chatbots, including claims of more transparent decision-making and stakeholder communication (IC2 via human interaction/transparency aspects).

title: Uncertainty quantification in real-time parameter updating for digital twins using Bayesian inverse mapping models
justification: Clearly about Digital Twins (real-time parameter updating for a DT) and discusses uncertainty quantification to support user trust and decision-making, which could relate to transparency/human interaction aspects. title: 3K: Knowledge-Enriched Digital Twin Framework
justification: Digital Twins are the central focus (3K framework) and the abstract explicitly motivates and targets "explainable inference mechanisms" for DT automated decision-making in critical infrastructure, satisfying IC1 and IC2.

justification: The study is clearly centered on a hybrid Digital Twin for damage identification (satisfies IC1). title: Generative AI in AI-Based Digital Twins for Fault Diagnosis for Predictive Maintenance in Industry 4.0/5.0
justification: Although it discusses Digital Twins and mentions XAI/human-centric aspects, the abstract indicates this paper presents the current state of the art and perspectives, suggesting it is a secondary study (survey/review), which meets EC3 for exclusion in Phase 1.

justification: Digital Twin is central (DT framework for IoT healthcare and virtual patient replica). justification: Digital Twin is central (a sequential deep reinforcement learning DT for personalized treatment outcomes), and the work explicitly addresses human-centered interaction and explainability via participatory design with oncologists and multiple visual explainability/XAI methods to promote trust and skepticism (IC1 + IC2).

title: AI Explainability Methods in Digital Twins: A Model and a Use Case
justification: Clearly centers on Digital Twins and explicitly addresses explainability via integrating XAI methods (XAI-DT system) to explain AI decisions to a human operator, including an architectural model and evaluation of explainability properties—meets IC1 and IC2.

title: Language Models for Functional Digital Twin of Circular Manufacturing
justification: Digital Twin is central ("Functional Digital Twin" for circular manufacturing). The work involves human interaction aspects by automatically pushing alerts to stakeholders and guiding upstream decision-makers, indicating human-centered decision support in the DT context.

title: A Blockchain-Assisted Federated Learning Framework for Secure and Self-Optimizing Digital Twins in Industrial IoT
justification: Digital Twins are a central focus (secure and self-optimizing DTs in IIoT), and the abstract explicitly mentions explainable AI (XAI) to enhance interpretability and transparency, satisfying IC1 and IC2.

title: Process Mining for Digital Twin Development of Industrial Cyber-Physical Systems
justification: The paper is explicitly about Digital Twin development for industrial cyber-physical systems (IC1) and directly discusses limited explainability impacting trustworthiness, proposing a framework to address this (IC2).

justification: The paper proposes a cognitive digital twin and explicitly includes an explainable AI (XAI) model to enhance transparency and trustworthiness for decision making, satisfying IC1 (Digital Twin central) and IC2 (explainability-related aspects).

justification: Digital Twin is central (immersive 3D digital twin for pipeline monitoring/training) and the work explicitly includes human interaction (embodied conversational agent) plus explainability aspects (agent can explain sensor anomalies; mentions explainable AI, trust, situational awareness, decision making).

justification: The paper explicitly frames LLMs as potential "human digital twins" and proposes a benchmark for simulating persona-based behavior chains, satisfying the Digital Twin relevance (IC1) in a broad sense. title: Towards a Digital Twin for Surgical Waiting List Management: A Preliminary Analysis and Design Study
justification: The paper centrally proposes a Digital Twin framework for surgical waiting list and hospital operations management (IC1) and explicitly emphasizes human-in-the-loop decision-making involving multiple stakeholders (human interaction aspect satisfying IC2).

title: An Overview of GenAI 2.0 Partnering With Digital Twin to Enhance Decision Making
justification: The title explicitly mentions partnering GenAI 2.0 with a Digital Twin (IC1). title: Generative and Predictive AI for digital twin systems in manufacturing
justification: Digital Twin is central (AI-enabled DT system for manufacturing). The abstract explicitly mentions envisioning Explainable AI (EAI) and emphasizes decision-support, which relates to explainability/human interaction aspects in DT context, satisfying IC1 and IC2 for Phase 1.

justification: Digital Twin is central (FL–DT framework and Streamlit-based DT platform for smart buildings). justification: The paper is explicitly about a semantic Digital Twin for construction safety (IC1) and emphasizes “explainable and verifiable inferences” plus auditability of decisions via ontology-based reasoning and compliance checking, directly relating to explainability/transparency in a Digital Twin context (IC2).

justification: Digital Twin is central (conceptual DT for food processing with layered architecture). It explicitly emphasizes interpretability and traceable insights to support root-cause analysis and operator decision-making, satisfying DT + explainability/human-interaction aspects (IC1, IC2).

justification: Directly focuses on Network Digital Twins and proposes integrating an XAI framework to enhance interpretability of a deep learning/GNN-based NDT, explicitly addressing explainability in the Digital Twin context (IC1 + IC2).

title: CogTwin: A Hybrid Cognitive Architecture Framework for Adaptable and Cognitive Digital Twins
justification: Digital Twins are the central focus (CogTwin framework for Cognitive Digital Twins) and the abstract explicitly mentions explainable AI (XAI) for transparency and human–CogTwin collaboration, satisfying IC1 and IC2.

title: Digital Twins and Virtual Assistants for Proactive Long-Term Care: The SALUS Architecture
justification: Digital twin technology is central (dual physical and psychological twins) and the architecture explicitly includes human interaction via an LLM-based virtual assistant plus explainable AI components to support caregiver decision-making, satisfying IC1 and IC2.

justification: Digital Twins are central (DT-based evaluation framework for CPPS using DT architectures and AAS). title: End-to-End Federated Intelligence for Secure and Standardized Digital Twin Orchestration in 6G Smart Cities
justification: Digital Twins are central (6G smart city DT orchestration architecture). The abstract explicitly mentions explainability-related aspects via “explainable AI audits” and AI governance/trust metrics, satisfying IC1 and IC2; not a secondary study.

justification: Digital twins are a central part of the proposed 6G LAN security framework (graph-based DTs). The paper explicitly includes an explainability module (SHAP) for transparent decision-making and mentions confidence-aware handling with human oversight, satisfying IC1 and IC2.

justification: Meets IC1 by proposing a Cognitive Digital Twin framework for solar PV infrastructure. title: AI-Driven Digital Twin for Condition Monitoring and Real-Time Fault Detection in PV Systems
justification: The paper proposes an AI-driven Digital Twin framework for PV condition monitoring (IC1) and explicitly emphasizes interpretable machine learning and an 'explainable solution' (IC2), indicating explainability/XAI aspects within the digital twin context.

justification: The paper is clearly centered on a Digital Twin Government paradigm (satisfies IC1) and uses LLMs/ontologies for semantic enrichment of tabular data. title: A Generative AI-Enhanced Digital Twin Framework for Heterogeneous Networks and Smart Environments
justification: The paper clearly centers on a Digital Twin framework for heterogeneous networks (IC1). title: Intelligent digital twin process for the end-milling simulation combined with a multi-physical model
justification: The article is centrally about a Digital Twin platform for machining (IC1) and explicitly discusses lack of interpretability in AI-based digital twins and the need for physics-based integration to enhance transparency and reliability (IC2).

title: Towards a client-based digital twin for decision making: a workforce integration use case
justification: Meets IC1 by proposing a Digital Twin concept (client-based DT) and meets IC2 via explicit human-centered decision-making and human–AI interaction through an LLM-supported chatbot providing support without replacing experts.

title: Bayesian Networks for data contextualization in Digital Twins of complex civil infrastructures
justification: Digital Twins are a central focus (DTs for complex civil infrastructures) and the abstract explicitly discusses lack of explainability in data-driven approaches and proposes Bayesian Networks to enhance interpretative capabilities and decision-support, addressing explainability/human decision alignment aspects (IC1 + IC2).

title: Digital Twins in Manufacturing: A Systematic Literature Review With Retrieval-Augmented Generation
justification: This is a systematic literature review (secondary study) about digital twins in manufacturing and does not mention explainability/interpretability/transparency or human interaction aspects in the abstract. It therefore clearly meets EC3 (secondary study) for Phase 1 exclusion.

title: Prescriptive Analytics for Next-Gen Supply Chains: Integrating Causal AI with Digital Twin Technologies
justification: The paper centrally integrates Digital Twin technologies with Causal AI in a supply-chain framework (IC1) and explicitly mentions decision explainability via causal/counterfactual reasoning for decision-makers (IC2).

title: An explainable digital twin framework for skin cancer analysis using early activation meta-learner
justification: The paper explicitly proposes a "digital twin framework" for virtual simulation and monitoring of the diagnostic process (IC1) and incorporates explainable AI methods to improve transparency and interpret model predictions (IC2).

title: DefectGPT: An Automatic Retrieval-Augmented Framework for Digital Twin-Based Defect Information Management and Analytics
justification: The paper centrally proposes a Digital Twin-based framework (DefectGPT) for building defect management (IC1) and explicitly involves human-facing decision support via an LLM providing insights/recommendations and mentions the need for "explainable" maintenance systems (IC2: human interaction/decision-making and explainability-related aspect).

title: Dynamic Incentive Strategies for Smart EV Charging Stations: A LLM-Driven User Digital Twin Approach
justification: The paper explicitly uses “user digital twins” (LLM-driven) in a smart EV charging/V2G demand-response framework (IC1). title: Generative AI-Assisted Digital Twin for Power Asset Management
justification: The article centrally proposes a Digital Twin framework for power asset management (IC1). title: Secure and decentralized digital twin optimization: A blockchain-enabled federated learning approach for IIoT
justification: Digital twins are the central focus (IIoT digital twin optimization). The abstract explicitly mentions transparency and explainability/interpretability and aims for trustworthy AI-driven decision-making, satisfying the requirement of DT relevance plus explainability-related aspects.

title: A Unifying Approach for Digital Twins in Healthcare: Perspectives and Experiences
justification: Directly focuses on Human Digital Twins in healthcare (IC1) and explicitly emphasizes the need for explainable and interpretable models to ensure trustworthiness, combining model-based and data-driven techniques leveraging explainability (IC2).

title: Critical Infrastructure Security through Digital Twin Synergy and Explainable Anomaly Detection
justification: The abstract centrally discusses integrating Digital Twins with explainable AI (XAI) for anomaly detection in critical infrastructure, explicitly emphasizing transparency and effective operator intervention. title: A Meta-model for Integrating Explainable Forecasting with Digital Twins
justification: Clearly centers on Digital Twins and explicitly integrates explainable forecasting, discussing human-in-the-loop needs for explainability and evaluating multiple explainability methods in a smart building digital twin, satisfying IC1 and IC2.

title: Enhancing Cybersecurity in Digital Twin Systems: Mitigating Challenges and Defending Against Threats
justification: Digital Twins are the central focus (DT cybersecurity systems/framework). title: Synergistic Interplay of Large Language Model and Digital Twin for Autonomous Optical Networks: Field Demonstrations
justification: Digital Twin is central (DT-enhanced LLM scheme for autonomous optical networks), satisfying IC1. title: Integration of Large Language Models and Digital Twins in the Public Sector
justification: The paper centrally discusses integrating Digital Twins with Large Language Models in the public sector (IC1). title: A User-in-the-loop Digital Twin for Energy Consumption Prediction in Smart Homes
justification: Digital Twin is central (smart home DT for energy consumption prediction) and the work explicitly adds user-in-the-loop interaction plus visualization features to explain predictions, warnings, and suggestions (explainable behavior), satisfying IC1 and IC2.

title: How Digital Twins Can Help to Accelerate the Transition to a Carbon-Neutral System
justification: Digital twins are a central concept (detailed physical simulation models called digital twins) applied to energy investment decisions, and the abstract explicitly discusses human/psychological aspects of decision making plus transparency and explainability as contributors to trust—meeting IC1 and IC2.

title: Digital Twins (Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning) for Diagnosis of Alzheimer’s Disease: Ethical and Regulatory Aspects

title: LLM-Based Adaptive Digital Twin Allocation for Microservice Workloads
justification: Digital Twins are a central component of the proposed DIRA-LDT framework for datacenter resource allocation (meets IC1). justification: Although it strongly involves Digital Twins and explainable AI, it is explicitly a comprehensive survey/secondary study (EC3), not a primary research article for inclusion in this phase.

justification: Digital Twin is central (building digital twin with self-evolution framework). title: Toward Cognitive Digital Twin System of Human–Robot Collaboration Manipulation

title: Harmfulness metrics in digital twins of social network rumors detection in cloud computing environment
justification: The title/abstract explicitly situate the work in a 'rumor detection digital twins' context (IC1). title: Vegetable Crop Growth Modeling in Digital Twin Platform Based on Large Language Model Inference
justification: The work clearly centers on a Digital Twin platform for crop growth modeling (IC1). title: Literacy Deep Reinforcement Learning-Based Federated Digital Twin Scheduling for the Software-Defined Factory

title: Explainable AI for cybersecurity automation, intelligence and trustworthiness in digital twin: Methods, taxonomy, challenges and prospects
justification: Although it is about Digital Twins and explainable AI, the article is explicitly an 'extensive study' providing methods/taxonomy/challenges—i.e., a survey/secondary study—so it meets EC3 (secondary studies) and should be excluded in Phase 1.

title: Digital Twins-enabled Zero Touch Network: A smart contract and explainable AI integrated cybersecurity framework
justification: Digital Twins are a core component of the proposed ZTN cybersecurity framework (DTs used to simulate attack detection/IDS development), and the paper explicitly addresses explainability via XAI/SHAP to improve transparency and accountability, satisfying IC1 and IC2.

title: Empowering digital twins with large language models for global temporal feature learning
justification: Centers on a Digital Twin multi-agent architecture driven by LLMs (DT is central) and explicitly addresses interpretability limitations, decision acceptability, user intervention barriers, and traceability—clear human-related and explainability/interpretability aspects in the DT context.

title: Survey and insights on digital twins design and smart grid's applications
justification: Although it is strongly about Digital Twins in smart grids and mentions human-in-the-loop aspects, the paper is explicitly a “comprehensive literature review” (survey), which is a secondary study and therefore excluded under EC3.

title: Explainable, interpretable, and trustworthy AI for an intelligent digital twin: A case study on remaining useful life
justification: Meets IC1 by centering on an intelligent Digital Twin for RUL prediction, and meets IC2 by explicitly focusing on explainable, interpretable, and trustworthy AI (XAI/IML), transparency, and user trust in the DT’s decision-making.

title: Proceedings - 2024 IEEE 4th International Conference on Digital Twins and Parallel Intelligence, DTPI 2024
justification: This record is a conference proceedings volume (134 papers) rather than an individual peer-reviewed primary study, making it a secondary/container publication. The abstract does not establish a specific Digital Twin + explainability/human-interaction focus for a single article (EC3).

title: HUMAN-IN-THE-LOOP DIGITAL TWIN FRAMEWORK FOR ERGONOMIC ASSESSMENT OF EXOSKELETONS IN CONSTRUCTION
justification: The paper proposes a “human-in-the-loop digital twin framework” for ergonomic risk assessment of exoskeletons, making Digital Twins central (IC1). It explicitly emphasizes human-in-the-loop aspects and decision-support visualization via a dashboard, satisfying the required human-centered/interaction component (IC2).

title: What does a Heart Beat for? A Heterogeneous Approach for Human Digital Twin Construction
justification: The paper explicitly targets construction of a Human Digital Twin (IC1) and emphasizes transparency/interpretability by combining data-driven and model-based methods so users can understand treatment effects (explainability and human interaction aspects; IC2).

title: Assessing Urban Safety: A Digital Twin Approach Using Streetview and Large Language Models
justification: The article explicitly uses a Digital Twin framework (IC1) combined with vision large language models for urban safety assessment. However, the abstract does not clearly mention explainability/interpretability/transparency or human-centered interaction aspects (IC2); it focuses on accuracy/validation and decision-making for planners. Potential relevance to human decision support exists but is not explicit, so keep as maybe for high-recall screening.

title: Artificial Intelligence-Powered Digital Twins for Sustainable and Resilient Engineering Structures
justification: Digital Twins are central (AI-powered DT framework for engineering structures), satisfying IC1. However, the abstract does not clearly mention explainability/interpretability/transparency or human-centered interaction aspects (IC2); it focuses on sensing/simulation/prediction and decision making without explicit XAI or human-in-the-loop discussion, so potential relevance remains but is unclear.

title: A Generative City Digital Twin System for Flooding Emergency Management in Smart City
justification: Digital Twin is central (auto-generative City Flooding Digital Twin for emergency management). The abstract explicitly mentions human-centered/interaction aspects (XR-based interaction, virtual-real interactive control, stakeholder decision-making) and evaluates interpretability and usability, meeting IC1 and IC2.

title: XAI-driven digital twin for cobot dynamic error compensation
justification: Clearly centers on a Digital Twin applied to cobot dynamic error compensation and explicitly addresses explainability via an XAI approach to produce human-comprehensible models, aligning with IC1 and IC2.

title: LLM experiments with simulation: Large Language Model Multi-Agent System for Simulation Model Parametrization in Digital Twins
justification: Digital Twins are central (LLM multi-agent framework for simulation model parametrization in digital twins). It also explicitly addresses human-centered aspects (improving usability, user-friendliness, reducing cognitive load, assisting decision-making), satisfying IC1 and IC2 (human interaction aspects) for Phase 1.

title: Dynamic Digital Twins for Situation Awareness
justification: Digital Twins are the central topic (dynamic DTs/DDDAS). The abstract explicitly discusses "trustworthy and explainable DTs (xDT)" and notes enhancing DT interpretability/explainability, satisfying IC1 and IC2.

title: CHATTWIN: ENABLING NATURAL LANGUAGE INTERACTIONS WITH INFRASTRUCTURE DIGITAL TWINS
justification: Digital Twin is central (infrastructure digital twins) and the work explicitly targets human interaction via natural language (LLM-based querying, user-centric interfaces, human-friendly outputs), satisfying IC1 and IC2 (human-centered interaction aspect).

title: Autonomous Human-Robot Collaborative Assembly Method Driven by the Fusion of Large Language Model and Digital Twin
justification: The paper explicitly uses a Digital Twin as part of an autonomous human-robot collaborative assembly method (IC1) and is strongly human-centered (human-robot collaboration, understanding human intention, operator action perception and task decision support), satisfying the Phase 1 requirement of DT relevance plus human interaction aspects (IC2).

title: AI-based traffic analysis in digital twin networks
justification: The chapter is explicitly about digital twin networks (Digital Twins) and discusses challenges including interpretability and strategies prioritizing transparency and accountability in AI-driven traffic analysis, satisfying IC1 and IC2.

title: From Simulation to Prediction: Enhancing Digital Twins with Advanced Generative AI Technologies
justification: Clearly centered on Digital Twins (IC1) and discusses LLM-based agents making DTs more interactive and supporting decision-making, which could imply human interaction aspects (IC2b). However, the abstract does not explicitly mention explainability/interpretability/transparency, so relevance to XAI is uncertain; retain for later-phase assessment.

title: An LLM-Based Digital Twin for Optimizing Human-in-the Loop Systems
justification: The title claims a “Digital Twin” and the abstract strongly emphasizes human-in-the-loop interaction (occupant preferences) using LLM agents, which aligns with human-centered aspects (IC2b). However, the abstract does not clearly describe a Digital Twin architecture (it reads more like an LLM-based simulator within a CPS/RL loop), and it does not mention explainability/interpretability explicitly. Given potential DT relevance plus clear HITL focus, retain for later-phase clarification.

title: Generative artificial intelligence of things systems, multisensory immersive extended reality technologies, and algorithmic big data simulation and modelling tools in digital twin industrial metaverse
justification: Although it discusses digital twins and mentions explainable AI, the abstract describes a PRISMA-based inspection of published research with systematic-review tools (AMSTAR, CASP, JBI, DistillerSR, etc.), indicating it is a secondary study/survey rather than primary research. This clearly meets EC3 (secondary study), so it should be excluded in Phase 1.

title: Enhancing Cognitive Digital Twin Interaction using an LLM Agent
justification: Digital Twin is central (cognitive digital twins of countries) and the architecture explicitly emphasizes human interaction via conversational interfaces plus “transparent and explainable insights,” directly meeting IC1 and IC2.

title: Explainable Data-Driven Digital Twins for Predicting Battery States in Electric Vehicles
justification: The article is centrally about Digital Twins for battery management in electric vehicles (IC1) and explicitly addresses explainability via XAI methods (SHAP, LIME, surrogate models) to make AI-based digital twin predictions trustworthy and interpretable (IC2).

title: Cognitive Digital Twins for Improving Security in IT-OT Enabled Healthcare Applications
justification: The article centrally discusses (Cognitive) Digital Twins and proposes a CDT-based adaptive cybersecurity framework. It explicitly mentions a human-in-the-loop decision-making approach and human factors within the DT framework, satisfying IC1 and the human-centered/interaction aspect under IC2.

title: Synergizing First-Principles and Machine Learning: Predicting Steel Flatness in the Era of Digital Twins and Physics-Informed Intelligence
justification: Mentions a “state-of-the-art digital twin structure” (IC1) and explicitly emphasizes “transparency and interpretability” of the predictive approach (IC2). Therefore it meets Phase 1 inclusion (Digital Twin + explainability-related aspects).

title: Harnessing Machine Learning, Blockchain, and Digital Twin Technology for Advanced Robotics in Manufacturing: Challenges and Future Directions
justification: The article explicitly discusses Digital Twin technology in manufacturing robotics (IC1) and mentions model interpretability as a challenge, plus transparency in the context of blockchain (potential IC2). However, the abstract does not clearly connect explainability/interpretability or human interaction aspects specifically to the Digital Twin component, so relevance to DT+XAI is plausible but unclear.

title: Digital Twin and Foundation Models: A New Frontier
justification: Digital Twin is central (integration of foundation models into DT solutions). The abstract explicitly mentions transparency in AI decision-making and interpretability/safety considerations, which relate to explainability/interpretability in the DT context (IC1 + IC2).

title: Reality anchor methodology: how to design a digital twin to support situation awareness
justification: Digital Twin is central (designing a DT as a decision support system). The work explicitly addresses human decision making and situation awareness, proposing a methodology with operator task analysis and human-in-the-loop testing—clear human-centered/interaction aspects relevant to explainability-related goals (supporting user understanding and projection of system state).

title: Enabling trustworthiness in human-swarm systems through a digital twin
justification: Digital twin is the central concept (a digital twin platform for human-swarm teaming) and the chapter explicitly addresses human interaction/trust requirements and a taxonomy for explainability, directly matching IC1 and IC2.

title: Blockchain-enabled digital twin system for brain stroke prediction
justification: The work clearly involves a Digital Twin, but the abstract focuses on prediction accuracy plus security/privacy via blockchain and anomaly correction, with no mention of explainability/interpretability/transparency/XAI or human-centered interaction aspects. This matches EC2 (DT used for predictive modeling without explainability or human-related aspects).

title: The Impact of Predictive Maintenance on the Performance of Industrial Enterprises
justification: The abstract focuses on predictive maintenance using IoT/AI/ML in an industrial company and does not mention Digital Twins or any explainability/interpretability/transparency or human-interaction aspects in a Digital Twin context (violates IC1; clear EC1 case).

title: Implementation of an AI-based predictive structural health monitoring strategy for bonded insulated rail joints using digital twins under varied bolt conditions
justification: Digital twin is used for AI-based predictive structural health monitoring and classifier performance, but the abstract contains no mention of explainability/interpretability/transparency/XAI or human-centered interaction aspects; it appears to focus exclusively on prediction/simulation within a digital twin (EC2).

title: A Symbolic AI Approach to Medical Training
justification: The paper presents a symbolic AI/simulation system (GLARE-Edu) for medical training based on clinical practice guidelines, but it does not mention Digital Twins or relate the work to Digital Twin concepts. Therefore it clearly fails IC1 and meets EC1 (unrelated to Digital Twins).

title: Digital Twin for Health Monitoring of a Cantilever Beam Using Support Vector Machine
justification: Although the paper clearly focuses on a Digital Twin framework for SHM (IC1), the abstract describes only predictive/classification performance using SVM and damage localization, with no mention of explainability/interpretability/transparency/XAI or human-centered interaction aspects (violates IC2; matches EC2).

title: Predecting power transformer health index and life expectation based on digital twins and multitask LSTM-GRU model
justification: The study proposes a monitoring architecture explicitly based on Fog Computing and Digital Twins for transformer health (IC1) and states that the framework incorporates model explanations with global and local explanations to support engineers (explainability/XAI aspect, IC2).

title: Feasibility of a clouds and edge computing scheme for internal due date assignment in advanced manufacturing systems
justification: The abstract discusses a cloud/edge computing scheme using DNN and random forest for due date assignment in manufacturing, with no mention of Digital Twins or twin-based architectures. It also does not address explainability/XAI or human-centered interaction in the context of Digital Twins. Therefore it clearly violates IC1 (and thus Phase 1 requirements), meeting EC1.

title: Deep learning based approaches for intelligent industrial machinery health management and fault diagnosis in resource-constrained environments
justification: The article is a survey on deep learning methods for industrial machinery health management (fault diagnosis, RUL prediction, edge-cloud architectures) and does not mention Digital Twins or discuss explainability/transparency/human interaction in the context of Digital Twins. It is also explicitly a secondary study (survey), which is excluded under EC3.

title: Optimized VMD and novel ECK-Venn based approach to IMF selection for chatter and tool wear classification
justification: The article focuses on signal processing and deep learning (VMD, IMF selection, spectrograms, CNN-MobileNet) for chatter and tool wear classification in machining, with no mention of Digital Twins or any explainability/transparency/human-interaction aspects in a Digital Twin context (violates IC1; clearly unrelated per EC1).

title: Research on the high precision hydraulic column stress monitoring method
justification: The abstract describes a high-precision stress monitoring and mapping method for hydraulic support columns in coal mines using data-driven and mechanism models, but it does not mention Digital Twins or any explainability/interpretability/human-interaction aspects in a Digital Twin context. This is clearly unrelated to Digital Twins (EC1).

title: A novel method for intelligent operation and maintenance of transformers using deep visual large model DETR + X and digital twin
justification: The article clearly uses Digital Twin as part of a framework/platform for transformer monitoring and maintenance (IC1). It also incorporates a fine-tuned LLaVA-7b expert decision-making tool that provides maintenance recommendations, indicating a human-facing decision support/interaction aspect. However, the abstract does not explicitly mention explainability/interpretability/transparency of the AI recommendations, so relevance to XAI is unclear (IC2), warranting a cautious 'maybe' in this high-recall phase.

title: Quantum machine learning for Lyapunov-stabilized computation offloading in next-generation MEC networks
justification: The title and abstract focus on quantum machine learning for computation offloading optimization in MEC networks using Lyapunov theory, with no mention of Digital Twins or any explainability/interpretability/human-interaction aspects in a Digital Twin context. This clearly violates IC1 (Digital Twin not discussed), so EC1 applies.

title: Towards Build Optimization Using Digital Twins - Proceedings of the 21st International Conference on Predictive Models and Data Analytics in Software Engineering
justification: Digital Twins are central (CI Build process Digital Twin framework), satisfying IC1. However, the abstract focuses on monitoring, ML modeling, what-if scenarios, and prescriptive services without explicit mention of explainability/interpretability/transparency or human-centered interaction aspects (IC2). Potential relevance could emerge in full text via user-facing monitoring/decision support, so prefer maybe in Phase 1.

title: Agentic AI for digital twin - Proceedings of the Thirty-Ninth AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Thirty-Seventh Conference on Innovative Applications of Artificial Intelligence and Fifteenth Symposium on Educational Advances in Artificial Intelligence
justification: Digital twin is central (agentic AI for digital twin in shipping). It explicitly emphasizes human interaction via a natural-language interface for diverse stakeholders (technicians to fleet managers) and interactive querying/decision support, satisfying the Phase 1 requirement of DT relevance plus human-centered/interaction aspects.

title: Data Storytelling to Unlock the Communicative Power of Digital Twins - Database and Expert Systems Applications: 36th International Conference, DEXA 2025, Bangkok, Thailand, August 25–27, 2025, Proceedings, Part II
justification: The paper is explicitly about Digital Twin systems and proposes a user-centered data storytelling workflow to make DT insights accessible, interpretable, and actionable for diverse audiences—addressing human-centered communication/interpretability aspects in the DT context (IC1 + IC2).

title: Toward Reliable Pavement Digital Twins: Multi-Scale Spatiotemporal Monitoring Challenges and Solutions - Proceedings of the 1st ACM SIGSPATIAL International Workshop on Spatial Intelligence for Smart and Connected Communities
justification: Digital Twins are central (pavement assets forming digital twins; proposed spatiotemporal framework). The abstract emphasizes reliability, uncertainty quantification, QA/QC, and decision support for agencies, which could relate to transparency/usability and human decision-making, but it does not explicitly mention explainability/XAI/interpretability or human-interaction aspects. Given potential relevance via uncertainty/verification and decision support, retain for later phases.

title: Digital Twins in Security Operations: State of the Art and Future Perspectives
justification: This is a structured literature review/survey of digital twins in security operations (secondary study of 201 publications), which falls under EC3. Although it mentions transparency in documenting data, it does not address explainability/XAI or human interaction aspects in the context of digital twins as required by IC2.

title: Large Language Models for Explainable Decisions in Dynamic Digital Twins - Dynamic Data Driven Applications Systems: 5th International Conference, DDDAS/Infosymbiotics for Reliable AI 2024, New Brunswick, NJ, USA, November 6–8, 2024, Proceedings
justification: The paper is explicitly about Dynamic Digital Twins and proposes using large language models to generate natural-language explanations of the twins’ autonomous decision-making, directly addressing explainability/human-understandable interaction (IC1 + IC2).

title: Nested Multi-objective Model Updating for an Aircraft Wingtail Digital Twin - Proceedings of the Genetic and Evolutionary Computation Conference Companion
justification: Although the paper is explicitly about a Digital Twin (aircraft wingtail FEM/ROM model updating), the abstract focuses exclusively on optimization, calibration, and computational efficiency/accuracy with no mention of explainability/interpretability/transparency or human-centered interaction aspects. This matches EC2 (DT predictive/simulation modeling without XAI or human-related aspects).

title: Robust and expert-agnostic digital twin calibration via ensemble learning and Bayesian optimization - Proceedings of the 12th ACM International Conference on Systems for Energy-Efficient Buildings, Cities, and Transportation
justification: The article is about digital twin calibration for building energy models using ensemble learning and Bayesian optimization, focusing on predictive robustness and parameter tuning. The abstract contains no mention of explainability/interpretability/transparency/XAI or human-centered interaction aspects, so it fits EC2 (DT predictive/simulation work without explainability or human-related aspects).

title: Semantic-aware LLM orchestration for proactive resource management in predictive digital twin vehicular networks
justification: The paper is clearly centered on Digital Twins (predictive DT for vehicular networks) and emphasizes human interaction via natural-language semantic commands and translating human intent into network behavior (IC1 + human-centered aspects). However, it does not explicitly mention explainability/interpretability/transparency/XAI, so relevance to explainability is indirect; retain for later phases.

title: Comparative Analysis of Motif-Based Anomaly Detection for Humidity Monitoring in Digital Twin Systems - Proceedings of the IEEE/ACM 12th International Conference on Big Data Computing, Applications and Technologies
justification: The paper is about motif-based anomaly detection for humidity monitoring in Digital Twin systems, but the abstract contains no mention of explainability, interpretability, transparency, XAI, or human-centered interaction aspects; it appears to focus exclusively on comparative predictive/detection methods (EC2).

title: FlexiDigital: A Comprehensive Approach to Energy Flexibility Services using Digital Twins and Large Language Models - Proceedings of the 16th ACM International Conference on Future and Sustainable Energy Systems
justification: Mentions Digital Twins as a core element (federated digital twins) and includes human-centered interaction aspects (citizen-driven services, AI-powered digital assistants, user engagement, prosumers controlling assets). However, the abstract does not explicitly mention explainability/interpretability/transparency, and it is a position paper (potentially still peer-reviewed in ACM proceedings), so it has potential relevance but is not clearly aligned with XAI from the abstract alone.

title: An X Language-Driven Framework for Systematic Development of Digital Twin Healthcare Systems
justification: Meets IC1 by focusing on Digital Twin Healthcare systems and a cloud DTH platform, and meets IC2 by explicitly addressing interpretability, trustworthiness, and transparency challenges of black-box AI within the digital twin, proposing a framework to develop interpretable and trustworthy DTH models.

title: The Role of Multi-Agents in Digital Twin Implementation: Short Survey
justification: Although it is clearly about Digital Twins, it is explicitly a short survey (secondary study), which meets EC3 for exclusion in Phase 1. The abstract also does not mention explainability/interpretability/transparency or human-centered interaction aspects in the DT context.

title: Optimizing Last-Mile Logistics with Digital Twins and Multi-agent Learning: Enhancing Efficiency, Customer Satisfaction, and Urban Integration
justification: Digital Twin is central to the proposed last-mile logistics framework (IC1). However, the abstract does not clearly mention explainability/interpretability/transparency or explicit human-centered interaction aspects; it references stakeholder benefits and consumer personalization options but without XAI or human-in-the-loop details. Potential relevance exists, so retain for later screening.

title: Opportunities for Digital Twins for the Provisioning, Management and Monitoring of Heterogeneous IoT Devices - Proceedings of the ACM/IEEE 27th International Conference on Model Driven Engineering Languages and Systems
justification: Digital Twins are a central concept (DT opportunities for managing IoT device lifecycles in a DaaS platform), satisfying IC1. However, the abstract does not clearly mention explainability/interpretability/transparency/XAI or explicit human-centered interaction aspects; it focuses on lifecycle management, requirements, and platform opportunities. Given potential for human interaction considerations in provisioning/management/monitoring, retain as maybe for high-recall screening.

title: Challenges and Opportunities in Secure Real-Time Digital Twin Systems for AR/VR-Enabled Smart Factories - Proceedings of the International Workshop on Middleware for IT/OT Integration
justification: Digital Twin is a central concept (real-time digital twin control architecture for smart factories). The abstract explicitly emphasizes human-machine collaboration and human-centric operator support via AR/VR and feedback loops, satisfying the requirement for human interaction aspects in the context of Digital Twins (even if explainability/XAI is not a main focus).

title: Explainable modeling in digital twin - Proceedings of the Winter Simulation Conference
justification: Clearly centered on Digital Twins and explicitly proposes an 'explainable modeling' framework with automatically generated explanations, explainability scores, and stakeholder collaboration/interaction to build trust—meeting IC1 and IC2.

title: Key technology of digital twin modeling for production process of flexible production line based on data - Proceedings of the 9th International Conference on Electronic Information Technology and Computer Engineering
justification: The paper is clearly about a Digital Twin framework for flexible production line modeling, monitoring, visualization, and simulation, but the abstract contains no mention of explainability/interpretability/transparency/XAI or human-centered interaction aspects beyond generic 'visual management.' This fits EC2 (DT focused on simulation/monitoring without explainability or human-related aspects).

title: How Digital Twins Can Help to Accelerate the Transition to a Carbon-Neutral System - Computer Aided Systems Theory – EUROCAST 2024: 19th International Conference, Las Palmas de Gran Canaria, Spain, February 25 – March 1, 2024, Revised Selected Papers, Part III
justification: Mentions using detailed physical simulation models as digital twins for renewable energy investment decisions (IC1) and explicitly discusses psychological aspects of decision making, highlighting trust, transparency, and explainability as key contributors (IC2).

title: Blockchain-Based Digital Twins: Research Trends, Issues, and Future Challenges
justification: Although it centrally discusses Digital Twins (blockchain-based DTs), it is explicitly a survey/review article (“In this survey… comprehensive review”), which is excluded under EC3 (secondary studies). It also does not mention explainability/interpretability or human-centered interaction aspects in the abstract.

title: Human-Autonomy Teaming on Autonomous Vehicles with Large Language Model-Enabled Human Digital Twins - Proceedings of the Eighth ACM/IEEE Symposium on Edge Computing
justification: The paper centers on a (human) digital twin for autonomous vehicles (IC1) and explicitly frames it within human-autonomy teaming and natural language interaction via LLMs (human-centered interaction aspects satisfying IC2).

title: How to regulate a Digital Twin City? Insights from a Proactive Law approach: How “human in the loop” and “precautionary principles” can serve policymakers in their attempt to incorporate respect of rights and solidarity in the smart city. - Proceedings of the 24th Annual International Conference ...
justification: Digital Twin City regulation is the central topic (IC1). The abstract explicitly discusses “human in the loop” and policymaker-oriented principles for incorporating rights/solidarity, indicating strong human-centered interaction/governance aspects in the context of digital twins (IC2).

title: Mathematical and Computational Foundations to Enable Predictive Digital Twins at Scale
justification: Digital Twins are the central focus (mathematical/computational foundations for predictive digital twins). The abstract explicitly mentions combining physics-based models with "interpretable machine learning techniques" and an "interpretable classifier," which satisfies the explainability/interpretability aspect required in Phase 1.

title: Explainable Online Lane Change Predictions on a Digital Twin with a Layer Normalized LSTM and Layer-wise Relevance Propagation - Advances and Trends in Artificial Intelligence. Theory and Practices in Artificial Intelligence: 35th International Conference on Industrial, E...
justification: Digital Twin is a central element (live data from a highway digital twin) and the work explicitly focuses on explainability (Layer-wise Relevance Propagation explanations for LSTM predictions) with a human-facing interface to communicate/explain predictions, satisfying IC1 and IC2.

title: Explainable Human-in-the-Loop Dynamic Data-Driven Digital Twins
justification: Clearly centers on Digital Twins and explicitly addresses explainability/interpretability and human-in-the-loop interaction (interpretable ML, goal modeling, trustworthiness of decisions) within DT/DDDAS systems, satisfying IC1 and IC2.

title: An Interpretable Digital Twin for Self-Aware Industrial Machines
justification: The paper centrally proposes a Digital Twin methodology for industrial machines and explicitly prioritizes interpretability and transparency (“interpretable digital twin”, “more transparent understanding”), directly meeting IC1 and IC2.

title: A Systematic Literature Review of Digital Twin Research for Healthcare Systems: Research Trends, Gaps, and Realization Challenges
justification: Although it is about Digital Twins, it is explicitly a systematic literature review (PRISMA-based). Phase 1 exclusion criterion EC3 excludes secondary studies such as systematic reviews or surveys, regardless of mentions of human-in-the-loop aspects.

title: TailorAlert: Large Language Model-Based Personalized Alert Generation System for Road Infrastructure Management with Digital Twins
justification: Digital Twins are central (road infrastructure management with DTs). The work explicitly targets human-centered interaction by generating role- and skill-tailored natural-language alerts for different personnel, improving decision-making and communication; this aligns with explainability/interpretability-related user-facing transparency needs even if not labeled as XAI.

title: An Efficient and Effective Cloud Monitoring Architecture based on Data Visualization and Digital Twin Technology
justification: The article centrally uses Digital Twin technology in a cloud monitoring architecture (IC1) and explicitly targets interpretability via data visualization plus an interactive digital twin and user studies (human interaction aspects), satisfying IC2 and the Phase 1 rule.

title: Empowering operators with a human-in-the-loop/on-the-loop simulation-based digital twin: the case of a smart learning factory
justification: The paper explicitly presents a simulation-based Digital Twin and emphasizes human-in-the-loop/on-the-loop operation via an interactive human-machine interface to support frontline workers’ decision-making (human-centered interaction). This satisfies IC1 and IC2 (human interaction aspects in the context of a Digital Twin).

title: Device Digital Twin Construction Based on Random Matrix Theory and Deep Auto-Encoder Networks
justification: Digital Twin is central (device-level digital twin construction for power systems). The framework explicitly provides "interpretable visualizations" and 3D visualizations to support decision-making, which relates to interpretability/transparency and human-centered interaction aspects (IC1 + IC2).

title: Automatically Learning Hybrid Digital Twins of Dynamical Systems
justification: While the paper is centrally about Digital Twins (hybrid DTs and automatic model generation), the abstract focuses on predictive/modeling performance (generalization, sample-efficiency, architecture search with LLMs) and does not mention explainability, interpretability, transparency, XAI, or human-centered/interaction aspects. This matches EC2 (DTs focused exclusively on modeling without explainability/human aspects).

title: Delving into the Digital Twin Developments and Applications in the Construction Industry: A PRISMA Approach
justification: Although it centrally discusses Digital Twins in construction, this is a PRISMA-based holistic review (secondary study), which clearly meets EC3. It also does not explicitly address explainability/interpretability/transparency or human-centered interaction in DTs beyond general decision-making.

title: From Digital Twins to Digital Selves and Beyond - Perspectives for Social Modelling in a Trans-Humanist World
justification: The abstract explicitly positions Digital Twins as baseline representations in cyber-physical systems and extends them to 'Digital Selves'. It also directly references transparency and an 'explainable knowledge base', indicating an explainability/XAI-related focus in the context of digital twin-like representations.

title: ENIGMA: An explainable digital twin security solution for cyber–physical systems
justification: Clearly centers on Digital Twins for CPS security and explicitly addresses explainability via an XAI-based DT security assessment model using SHAP; also involves human interaction/training of security analysts through gamification, satisfying IC1 and IC2.

title: Exploring digital twins: Attributes, challenges and risks
justification: Digital Twins are the central focus (attributes, challenges, risks). The abstract explicitly highlights explainability-related aspects such as "Transparency" and "Interpretability" and also mentions interactions with physical assets and co-creation with clients (human/interaction aspects), satisfying IC1 and IC2.

title: A discussion about the qualification of digital twins for maintenance models
justification: Digital twins are central (qualification for maintenance models). The paper explicitly targets trustworthiness and proposes a methodology to ensure quality, credibility, and interpretability of DTs, aligning with explainability/interpretability aspects (IC1 + IC2).

title: Big Data in Earth system science and progress towards a digital twin
justification: Although it discusses progress toward a digital twin of Earth, this is explicitly a Review article (secondary study), which meets Phase 1 exclusion criterion EC3.

title: Feasibility of Digital Twins to Manage the Operational Risks in the Production of a Ready-Mix Concrete Plant
justification: Digital Twin is central (proposes a DT system for ready-mix concrete plant risk management). It also references human-centered decision support via an analytical dashboard and explicitly mentions providing "interpretable" predictive maintenance insights, aligning with explainability/interpretability aspects in a DT context.

title: Digital Twin – Integrated Geomonitoring
justification: Digital Twin is the central concept ("Digital Twin – Integrated Geomonitoring" project) and the abstract explicitly mentions presenting results "in a transparent way" and providing "more transparency" for understanding environmental transformation processes, indicating transparency/human-understanding aspects in the context of a Digital Twin.

title: Literature Research on the Use and Requirements of Datagram Communication and Protocols in AAS and Digital Twins
justification: Digital Twins are central (AAS as a Digital Twin; protocols for DT systems). The abstract mentions an 'interpretability goal' in relation to communication protocols, but it is unclear whether this refers to XAI/explainability or merely technical interoperability/readability, and there is no explicit human-centered/interaction discussion. Potential relevance to transparency/interpretability warrants retention at Phase 1.

title: CONCEPTUAL ARCHITECTURE OF DIGITAL TWIN WITH HUMAN-IN-THE-LOOP -BASED SMART MANUFACTURING
justification: Clearly centers on a Digital Twin conceptual architecture and explicitly emphasizes human-in-the-loop, collaborative decision-making, and immersive human interaction (extended reality) in smart manufacturing, satisfying IC1 and IC2 (human-centered aspects).

title: Enhancing Digital Twins with Advances in Simulation and Artificial Intelligence: Opportunities and Challenges
justification: The article is centrally about Digital Twins and explicitly discusses challenges/opportunities of combining DTs with AI, including developing trustworthy and explainable AI methods. This satisfies IC1 (Digital Twin central) and IC2 (mentions explainable AI).

title: A General Framework for Human-in-the-Loop Cognitive Digital Twins
justification: Digital Twins (specifically Cognitive Digital Twins) are the central concept, and the abstract explicitly emphasizes human-in-the-loop involvement and the role of explainability/rationale in decision-making, satisfying IC1 and IC2.

title: Toward Digital Twins for Human-in-the-loop Systems: A Framework for Workload Management and Burnout Prevention in Healthcare Systems
justification: Digital Twin is central (conceptual HITL workload DT framework for healthcare systems). It explicitly focuses on human-in-the-loop aspects (provider workload, feedback mechanisms, burnout prevention), satisfying DT relevance plus human-centered interaction aspects required for Phase 1.

title: Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) Empowered Digital Twin on Soil Carbon Emission Management Using Proximal Sensing
justification: Clearly centers on a Digital Twin framework for soil carbon emissions (IC1) and explicitly addresses explainability/interpretability and transparent decision-making via XAI (IC2), including mention of human interaction in the DT context.
